chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever drinks a draught of wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking wine on one's prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific legal ruling where the consumption of wine (khamr) results in the non-acceptance of prayers for forty days, reflecting the severity of the sin in Shia jurisprudence. The duration of forty days is significant in Islamic tradition, often associated with periods of purification or divine decree, underscoring the spiritual impurity caused by intoxicants. This ruling highlights the direct link between physical consumption of haram substances and the validity of ritual worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who drinks a drink from wine, his Prayer would not be Accepted from him for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one drinks one sip of wine his Salat (prayer) is not accepted for forty days.’”
